qs.q: A part selected for testing is equally likely to have been produced on any one of six cutting tools. The probability that the part is from tool 3 or tool 5?
hints: All outcomes are equally likely, so count favourable outcomes.
Count the tools that satisfy the condition and divide by the total number of tools.
For equally likely outcomes, $P(E)=\dfrac{\text{number of outcomes in }E}{\text{total number of outcomes}}$.
steps: Tools 3 and 5 are mutually exclusive outcomes, so add: $\frac16+\frac16$.

qs.q: The analysis of shafts for a compressor is summarized by conformance to specification. \[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Round conforms} & \\ \hline \text{Surface finish conforms} & \text{Yes} & \text{No}\\ \hline \text{Yes} & 345 & 5\\ \text{No} & 12 & 8\\ \hline \end{array}\] If a shaft is selected at random, what is the probability that the selected shaft conforms to surface finish requirements or to roundness requirements?
hints: This asks for the probability of a union of two events.
Either add the probabilities and subtract the overlap, or take 1 minus the probability of failing both.
$P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)=1-P(A'\cap B')$.
steps: Let $A$ be surface finish conforms and $B$ be round conforms. Only the cell No/No (8 shafts) fails both.

qs.q: The analysis of shafts for a compressor is summarized by conformance to specification. \[\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline & \text{Round conforms} & \\ \hline \text{Surface finish conforms} & \text{Yes} & \text{No}\\ \hline \text{Yes} & 345 & 5\\ \text{No} & 12 & 8\\ \hline \end{array}\] If a shaft is selected at random, what is the probability that the selected shaft conforms to surface finish requirements given that it does not conform to roundness requirements?
hints: This is a conditional probability, so restrict attention to the given group.
Look only at the column of shafts that do not conform to roundness and find the share that conform to surface finish.
$P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$.
steps: Of these, surface finish conforms for 5 shafts.

qs.q: A lot of 100 semiconductor chips contains 20 that are defective. Two are selected randomly, without replacement, from the lot. What is the probability that both are defective?
hints: Use the multiplication rule for dependent draws.
Find the probability the first chip is defective, then the probability the second is defective given that the first was.
$P(A\cap B)=P(A)\,P(B\mid A)$.
steps: After removing one defective chip, $P(\text{2nd defective}\mid\text{1st})=\frac{19}{99}$.

qs.q: The following circuit operates if and only if there is a path of functional devices from left to right. The probability that each device functions is as shown. Assume that the probability that a device is functional does not depend on whether or not other devices are functional. What is the probability that the circuit operates?
hints: The circuit is two parallel pairs connected in series, and the devices are independent.
Find the probability that each parallel pair passes current, then combine the two pairs.
Parallel: $P=1-\prod(1-p_i)$. Series: $P=\prod p_i$ (independent devices).

qs.q: Let $f(x)=c\left(\frac12\right)^x$, $x=1,2,3$. Determine the value of the constant $c$ so that the function $f(x)$ satisfies the conditions of being a probability mass function.
opts: There is no $c$ satisfies the conditions of being a probability mass function
hints: A probability mass function must have probabilities summing to 1.
Add $f(1)+f(2)+f(3)$ in terms of $c$ and set the sum equal to 1.
A pmf requires $f(x)\ge0$ and $\sum_x f(x)=1$.
This is a conditional probability for a discrete variable.
The intersection of $\{X>1\}$ and $\{X<3\}$ is a single value; list the values in the condition.
$P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$ and $P(X\in S)=\sum_{x\in S}f(x)$.

qs.q: In a NiCd battery, a fully charged cell is composed on Nickelic Hydroxide. Nickel is an element that has multiple oxidation states that is usually found in the following states: \[\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \text{Nickel Charge} & \text{Proportion found}\\ \hline 0 & 0.17\\ +2 & 0.35\\ +3 & 0.33\\ +4 & 0.15\\ \hline \end{array}\] The probability of the positive nickel-charged options within one standard deviation from the mean
hints: Find the mean and standard deviation of the discrete distribution, then see which charges fall in the interval.
Compute $E(X)$ and $E(X^2)$, then $\sigma$, and form the interval $\mu\pm\sigma$. Keep only the positive charges inside it.
$\mu=\sum xf(x)$, $\sigma^2=\sum x^2f(x)-\mu^2$.
steps: The interval is $(1.055,\,3.525)$; the positive charges inside it are $+2$ and $+3$.

qs.q: Each sample of water has a $10\%$ chance of containing a particular organic pollutant. Assume that the samples are independent with regard to the presence of the pollutant. Find the probability that in the next 18 samples, at least three samples contain the pollutant.
hints: Count the samples containing the pollutant among a fixed number of independent trials.
Identify $n$ and $p$, then use the complement of "two or fewer".
$P(X=x)=\binom nx p^x(1-p)^{n-x}$ and $P(X\ge k)=1-P(X\le k-1)$.

qs.q: Errors in an experimental transmission channel are found when the transmission is checked by a certifier that detects missing pulses. The number of errors found in an eight-bit byte is a random variable with the following distribution \[ F(x)=\begin{cases}0, & x<1\\ 0.7, & 1\le x<4\\ 0.9, & 4\le x<7\\ 1, & x\ge7\end{cases} \] Then $P(X>3)=$
hints: Use the cumulative distribution function and the complement rule.
Write $P(X>3)$ as 1 minus a value of $F$.

qs.q: The number of errors in a textbook follows a Poisson distribution with a mean of 0.01 error per page. What is the probability that there are three or less errors in 100 pages?
hints: Counting events over a fixed amount of text with a known rate: a Poisson model.
Scale the rate to 100 pages first, then add the probabilities for 0 to 3 errors.
$P(X=x)=\dfrac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^x}{x!}$, and the mean scales with the length of the interval.

qs.q: A sample of size eight measurements were made on the inside diameter of forged piston rings used in an automobile engine. The data (in millimeters) are 74.001, 74.002, 74.014, 74.002, 74.005, 74.002, 74.005, and 74.004. If $A$ is the estimator of the population mean, $B$ is the estimator of the population standard deviation, then $A-B$ is given by
hints: The usual estimators are the sample mean and the sample standard deviation.
Compute $\bar x$, then $s$ with divisor $n-1$, and subtract.
$\bar x=\dfrac1n\sum x_i$ and $s=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sum(x_i-\bar x)^2}{n-1}}$.

qs.q: The following data on the motor fuel octane ratings of several blends of gasoline: \[ 82,\ 83,\ 85,\ 85,\ 86,\ 87,\ 87,\ 89,\ 89,\ 89,\ 89,\ 89,\ 90,\ 90,\ 91,\ 92,\ 94,\ 94,\ 96,\ 98 \] The $90^{th}$ percentile equal to
hints: Locate the position of the 90th percentile in the ordered data and interpolate.
The data are already sorted; count them, find the position of the percentile and interpolate between the two neighbouring values.
Position of the $100p$-th percentile (the $n+1$ convention): $p(n+1)$; if not an integer, interpolate between the neighbouring ordered values.
steps: Position $=0.9(21)=18.9$, between the 18th value $94$ and the 19th value $96$.

qs.q: You are told that the minimum, $1^{st}$, $2^{nd}$, $3^{rd}$ quartiles and the maximum for a set of 100 distance (in meters) achieved by a particular brand of golf ball in the overall distance test are 210, 251, 260, 275 and 295. Which of the following statements is true?
opts: The data contain outliers because the minimum distance is less than the limit for outliers
The data contain outliers because the maximum distance is more than the limit for outliers
The right whisker is longer than the left whisker
The inter quartile range is approximately 10 yards
hints: Use the box plot outlier fences built from the quartiles.
Compute the IQR, then the lower and upper fences, and compare them with the minimum and maximum.
$\text{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1$; outliers lie below $Q_1-1.5\,\text{IQR}$ or above $Q_3+1.5\,\text{IQR}$.
steps: The minimum $210<215$, so there are outliers on the low side; the maximum $295<311$ is not an outlier.
The IQR is 24, not about 10, and the left tail ($251-210=41$) exceeds the right ($295-275=20$), so the data are not symmetric and the right whisker is not longer. Only the first statement is true.
qs.brief: IQR $=24$: lower limit $215>210$, so the minimum is an outlier.
